calculationModel.formulaPlainEnglish: After verifying the executed abatement agreement, granting-authority resolution, ALDOR certificate package, certificate dates, qualifying invoices, and local/state rate split, savings equals the tax actually abated on qualifying incorporated project purchases. Use the qualifying capitalizable tangible personal property and taxable-service base within the certificate/project period, capped by the documented approved amount rules. Multiply that base by the documented abatable rate: state sales/use rate minus the documented unabated state portion, plus local sales/use tax not earmarked for education. Exclude the 0.75% state portion where applicable, local education taxes, nonqualifying purchases, purchases before the grant date, and purchases after the project is placed in service or the certificate expires.

calculationModel.formulaPlainEnglish: After the county approval and funding gates are satisfied, calculate the annual credit for the selected track. Green Business real property equals the eligible county real property tax base multiplied by 100%, 80%, 60%, 40%, or 20% for credit years 1 through 5. Green Business personal property equals the eligible county personal property tax base multiplied by 50% for credit years 1 through 5. High Performance Building new construction, major renovation, core-and-shell, NGBS, or equivalent equals the eligible county real property tax base multiplied by 25% for Silver, 50% for Gold, or 75% for Platinum or Emerald for 5 years. The County application supplies the operational percentages: Green Business real property 100%, 80%, 60%, 40%, and 20% for years 1-5, and Green Business personal property 50% for years 1-5. County high-performance materials supply the new-or-major renovation rates of 25%, 50%, and 75% for 5 years and existing-building O+M rates of 10%, 25%, and 50% for 3 years, with October 1 filing and a $5,000,000 fiscal-year aggregate cap. ([Prince George's County Government][1])

calculationModel.formulaPlainEnglish: For a County-approved application and a verified current County property tax bill or assessor allocation, calculate the current-tax-year credit for the approved path. Solar and geothermal are one-time residential-dwelling credits equal to the lesser of the statutory cost-based amount, $2,500, the dwelling-only County tax excluding land, and remaining County tax liability. High-performance building credits are annual building-only credits for up to five taxable years beginning with the approval year, using rating-specific rates and caps, limited by remaining County tax liability. Do not project future high-performance annual amounts unless each year’s official tax inputs are supplied.
calculationModel.formulaAmountCents: solar_or_geothermal_current_year_amount_cents = min(max(0, floor(total_paid_cost_cents / 2) - required_grant_and_state_credit_reduction_cents), 250000, county_dwelling_tax_excluding_land_cents, remaining_county_property_tax_liability_cents). high_performance_current_year_amount_cents = min(floor(county_building_tax_excluding_land_cents * rating_rate), rating_cap_cents, remaining_county_property_tax_liability_cents) when current_tax_year is approval_year through approval_year+4.
implementationNotes: This is not a free-form estimate. The executable model should be allowed, but positive inclusion must be gated by the County approval document and official County tax bill or assessor allocation.

For solar/geothermal, calculate the statutory amount as max(0, floor(total_paid_cost_cents / 2) - required_grant_and_state_credit_reduction_cents), then apply the $2,500, dwelling-tax-only, and remaining-liability caps.
For high-performance, calculate only the current tax year’s annual credit unless a schedule of official tax inputs is available for multiple years.
If the approved credit path and user-selected path disagree, use the official County approval document and treat the user-selected path as non-authoritative.

rules.evidenceText: Anne Arundel County states its credits reduce County property taxes, do not affect other charges, cannot exceed actual tax liability, and require building/dwelling-versus-land treatment for these programs. County forms and code excerpts provide the solar one-time lesser-of formula capped at $2,500, the geothermal one-time lesser-of formula capped at $2,500, and the high-performance residential and commercial rating percentages and dollar caps for a five-year building-only credit. County materials also state high-performance building credits cannot be combined with other optional credits, while total credits cannot exceed property tax liability. ([Anne Arundel County Government][2])

rules.jurisdictionText: New York State municipalities and school districts under RPTL §487

gateConditions: pilot_notice_pilot_agreement_or_official_confirmation_that_no_pilot_is_required documents either no PILOT or the annual PILOT payment for the estimate year
calculationModel.formulaPlainEnglish: For each estimate year during the approved 15-year exemption term, use the assessor-approved exempt assessed value for the eligible system. For each overlapping taxing jurisdiction that has not opted out for the applicable technology category, multiply that exempt assessed value by the jurisdiction's current property-tax rate normalized as dollars per $1,000 of assessed value. Sum the eligible jurisdiction tax effects, excluding special ad valorem levies and special assessments, then subtract the documented annual PILOT payment for that estimate year. If no PILOT is required, the PILOT offset is zero. Do not calculate any nonzero customer value until the assessor approval/exempt-value gate, opt-out gate, tax-rate gate, and PILOT/no-PILOT gate are satisfied.
calculationModel.formulaAmountCents: amount_cents = max(0, Σ_j(round(exempt_assessed_value_cents * tax_rate_per_1000_assessed_value_j / 1000)) - min(documented_annual_pilot_payment_cents_for_estimate_year, Σ_j(round(exempt_assessed_value_cents * tax_rate_per_1000_assessed_value_j / 1000)))) for jurisdictions j where official opt_out_status_j == false and levy line applies to RPTL §487; otherwise 0 or blocked_zero.
implementationNotes: Add ny_rptl_487_property_tax_exemption as a gated property-tax exemption method; do not route this rule to any existing sales/use or income-tax-credit runtime method.
The method may include a user-facing annual value only when the gate inputs are present; otherwise keep customerFacingSavingsCents at 0 and surface blocked_for_assessor_tax_bill_or_pilot_input.

For the Albany synthetic fixture, the expected annual amount is 142766 cents: assessor-approved exempt assessed value 3800000 cents times combined rate 37.57 dollars per $1000 assessed value divided by 1000, less 0 PILOT.
Use per-jurisdiction rates internally even when a combined rate is displayed, because opt-out status and PILOT offsets can vary by jurisdiction.

rules.evidenceText: RPTL §487 exempts eligible energy systems from taxation to the extent of the increase in assessed value attributable to the system for 15 years, requires owner application on the prescribed form by taxable status date, allows local opt-out by counties, cities, towns, villages, and school districts by technology category, and allows solar or wind PILOT treatment in non-opt-out jurisdictions. The Tax Department publishes an official list of filed local laws and resolutions, with the reviewed list showing records on file as of March 31, 2026. Form RP-487 and its instructions provide the assessor-facing incremental-cost calculation and filing workflow. ([NY Tax Department][3])
rules.reasoningNotes: Promote as a safe assessor/PILOT workflow rather than a deterministic statewide savings calculator. The statutory formula is source-backed, but parcel-level savings depend on assessor-approved exempt assessed value, overlapping taxing jurisdictions, opt-out status, PILOT status, and current tax rates.

calculationModel.formulaPlainEnglish: For each eligible tax year, use the assessor-certified exempt assessed value or official solar tax-credit bill line after any local partial-exemption percentage has already been applied. If an official bill-specific solar credit amount is present, use that amount. Otherwise, annual benefit equals the assessor-certified exempt value multiplied by the applicable local tax rate per $100 of assessed value, divided by 100. Generate the benefit only for the certified start year through the certified term. Alexandria's verified term is 5 years; City of Fairfax's verified term is 10 years. Other Virginia localities require an official local subrule or assessor document before any nonzero value.
calculationModel.formulaAmountCents: annualBenefitCents = official_bill_solar_credit_amount_cents if present; else roundHalfUp(assessor_certified_exempt_value_cents * applicable_tax_rate_per_100_assessed_value / 100). Example using the supplied Alexandria synthetic profile: roundHalfUp(19925000 * 1.135 / 100) = 226149 cents.

calculationModel.formulaPlainEnglish: After documented County approval and funding, calculate one approved property line at a time. calculationModel.formulaPlainEnglish: With all official gates satisfied, compute the annual benefit from documented eligible tax lines only. For each eligible line, use the documented post-RERZ tax if available; otherwise multiply the documented pre-RERZ eligible tax amount by the approved RERZ savings multiplier. Exclude federal taxes, Corporate Income Tax, local bond obligations, school sinking fund, special assessments, sales/use tax, and any line not identified as RERZ-eligible. Before the final three years the standard savings multiplier is 1.00; in the final three years the standard savings multipliers are 0.75, 0.50, and 0.25, unless the official tax document provides a more specific documented line result.

rules.evidenceText: ORC 5751.03 imposes CAT at two and six-tenths mills per dollar on taxable gross receipts after subtracting the exclusion amount, applies the full exclusion to the first calendar-quarter return, and carries unused exclusion forward to later quarters in the same year. ([Ohio Laws][12]) ORC Chapter 5751 states that CAT is levied on each person with taxable gross receipts for the privilege of doing business in Ohio, provides quarterly filing mechanics, and requires the fourth-quarter return to adjust over- or under-reported receipts for the calendar year. ([Ohio Laws][13]) Ohio's official CAT information release states that the annual minimum tax is eliminated for periods beginning January 1, 2024, the exclusion is $3,000,000 in 2024 and $6,000,000 in 2025 and thereafter, the 0.26% rate is unchanged, annual filing is eliminated after the 2023 return, taxpayers at or below the threshold are not required to file, and combined/consolidated groups are treated as one taxpayer. ([Cloudinary][14]) Ohio's official update for Q2 2025 confirms the $6,000,000-or-less cancellation message and electronic filing/payment routing through the Ohio Business Gateway. ([GovDelivery][15])
rules.reasoningNotes: Promote the current CAT constants and mechanics, but keep runtime status as needs_tax_return because a customer-facing amount requires the taxpayer's current return period, Ohio taxable gross receipts, group status, used exclusion, and account/filing status.
